paper.title_en: Detection of a warm absorber in a highly variable low-redshift quasar
paper.abstract_en: { 3XMMJ115535.8+232723 (z=0.136) is a low-redshift radio-quiet quasar, which shows an unusual spectral nature. The X-ray properties and variability of this source have never been studied.} {Using numerous X-ray observations, this study aims to perform a detailed spectral analysis for 3XMMJ115535.8+232723. Having produced spectra from different flux states, the aims of the study is to investigate long-term spectral behaviour in a single object outside the local group of AGNs.} { We used {\it XMM-Newton} and {\it Chandra} observations of quasar 3XMMJ115535.8+232723 obtained between 2000 and 2008 to derive the spectroscopic details. We analyzed 0.3--10 keV spectra using an absorbed powerlaw model in combination with a warm absorber component.} {The first spectroscopic analysis of 3XMMJ115535.8+232723 reveals that the X-ray spectrum imprints a strong absorption feature, prominent at $\sim 0.7$ keV, which has been interpreted to be due to absorption in a partially ionized material (a.k.a. warm absorber). The column density and ionization parameter of the warm absorber vary by more than an order of magnitude for different observations. The results are consistent with high density clouds located ($\sim 1000$ gravitational radius) from the central region and another set of low density clouds further away. The intrinsic flux and spectral shape of the source also varies significantly over the observations.}
